questions.title: Which former minister from Viktor Orban's government, if any, will have parliamentary immunity lifted in September 2026 to permit an embezzlement investigation?
questions.background: The party that won Hungary's 2026 parliamentary election campaigned on tackling corruption. Parliamentary immunity can prevent prosecutors from pursuing criminal investigations against legislators unless Parliament lifts it.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Hungarian parliamentary records or contemporaneous reporting from reliable news organizations identifying former ministers whose immunity is lifted. Qualifying Event : Hungary's Parliament must vote during September 2026 to remove a former Orban-government minister's immunity specifically to allow prosecutors to pursue an embezzlement investigation. Allegations alone, without the parliamentary vote, do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : Provide the former minister's full name. If no former minister qualifies during September 2026, resolve as no qualifying minister.

questions.title: Which activist detained in Tunisia's Global Sumud Flotilla fundraising case will suspend his hunger strike between September 12 and September 27, 2026?
questions.background: Four activists have been detained since March in a Tunisian investigation into alleged financial irregularities involving fundraising for the Global Sumud Flotilla, an international campaign seeking to deliver aid to Gaza. Hunger strikes are being used to protest their continued detention.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera identifying which of the four detained activists has suspended his hunger strike. Resolution Conditions : The suspension must have occurred between September 12 and September 27, 2026, inclusive. Appeals to suspend the strike or statements of future intention do not count. Accepted Answer Format : The activist's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: 2026-09-20 update (Al Jazeera Sept 20 — explicit Source of Truth — and Roots TV Sept 18): Al Jazeera's Tunis report today confirms NONE of the four detained Global Sumud Flotilla activists has suspended his hunger strike yet following Saturday's Tunis solidarity protest ('remain determined to continue their hunger strike until their release'). Crucially, Al Jazeera reports Wael Naouar has now reached ~35 days on hunger strike (since Aug 16), suffering repeated fainting, difficulty breathing, hallucinations, and >20kg (44lb) weight loss ('real danger threatening him'), whereas the other three only joined on Sept 9 (~Day 11 today, 24 days behind Naouar; Henchiri still urgently needs surgery for a prior injury in Israel, keeping him clear #2). With the Sept 12-27 window now past its midpoint (only 7 days remaining, resolution_date Sept 23) and Naouar entering acute medical danger while co-detainees are at Day 11, nudging Wael Naouar 0.81 -> 0.84 (strictly within the 0.85 cap) and trimming Ghassan Henchiri (0.07), Nabil Channoufi (0.045), and Ghassan Boughdiri (0.045). Note: Al Jazeera used 'Ghassen' in today's bylined piece vs 'Ghassan' in its Sept 2 and Sept 10 reports, while 'Wael Naouar' and 'Nabil Channoufi' are identical across all three; retaining 2/3 Al Jazeera house spellings.
